system.description:
Network represents the geographical extent of a Setite's web of contacts, allies, and retainers. Each dot of Network expands the Setite's reach, though it does not by itself increase the number of members in the network — the player must still purchase dots of Allies, Contacts, Herd, or Retainers, representing servitors readily at hand (usually in the Setite's home city).

When the Setite arrives in a new locale covered by his Network, a similar number of Allies, Contacts, Herd, and Retainers become available there; the Setite never permanently loses dots in those Backgrounds by traveling within his web of influence. On arriving in another city within the Network, the moved Backgrounds become available at a rate of three dots per night, in whatever order the player chooses.

The Setite may also reach members of his network in another city by message, or through the Immanence of Set power Whisper of the Sands. Without his physical presence, however, network members can only serve as Contacts (information only) — a master must be close at hand to command services beyond information-gathering.

  • 1 dot: The network covers two distinct cities.
  • 2 dots: The network covers three distinct cities.
  • 3 dots: The network covers a small geographical region (such as the Nile Delta) or four distinct cities. At three or more dots, the Storyteller may allow the network to spread across a region instead of being fixed to specific cities.
  • 4 dots: The network covers a significant region (such as Upper Egypt or the Languedoc) or five distinct cities.
  • 5 dots: The network covers a large geographic area (such as Egypt, France, or the Low Countries) or six distinct cities.
system.source: Libellus Sanguinis III: Wolves at the Door, Book Three
